data.description:
## Problem
A misleading error code is a significant failure mode: it causes LLM/agent consumers to make erroneous assumptions and act on a wrong diagnosis (e.g. "the AI provider is down" when the real fault is bad input or a missing asset). Recent bugs are all instances of ONE systemic pattern: the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` fallthrough in the workflow `error_code_for` classifier mislabels non-LLM failures.

Known instances: 35ab (unknown-step -> llm_unavailable, FIXED -> invalid_input), 551b (missing-bundle -> llm_unavailable, DEFERRED/latent), 73d8 (ExpressionError -> llm_unavailable, pending design decision).

## Goal
Systematically audit EVERY error-code / classification surface so each returned code accurately and specifically describes the actual condition, and no failure degrades to a misleading catch-all.

## Scope (surfaces to enumerate)
- Workflow error-code vocabulary + `error_code_for` mapping (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py`) — esp. the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` fallthrough branch.
- The 8-class LLM `ResolutionClass` disposition taxonomy (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py`).
- Top-level `_errors.py`, `_mcp_errors.py`, exit-code maps, and any other error-code producer.

## Acceptance criteria
- A complete inventory of every error code and every mapping/fallthrough that can produce it.
- Each mapping labeled: accurate, MISLEADING (wrong code for the condition), or lossy catch-all.
- Every MISLEADING/lossy mapping gets a child ticket: observable -> bug to fix; latent -> documented + deferred; needs-new-vocabulary or behavior-change -> escalate as a design decision.
- A recommended guardrail (test/lint/review criterion) that would catch a new misleading mapping before it ships (prevention).
- 73d8 and 551b linked in as instances of this epic.

## Constraints
Read-only audit first (no code changes, no LLM gate ops during the active load-shed). Remediation lands via Gerrit per AGENTS.md after the incident fix lifts the load-shed. No --force.
data.title: Audit all error codes for descriptiveness; eliminate misleading classifications
